articles.title: DR Congo’s deadliest Ebola outbreak kills over 4,200 as armed groups undermine response
articles.author: Pavan Kulkarni
articles.content_excerpt: In less than five months, the fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak in world history has killed at least 4,205 people in the conflict-ridden eastern region of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) as of October 7. It is the deadliest outbreak in the DRC since the disease was first discovered in the country in 1976, killing nearly one in two of the 8,728 people confirmed to be infected. With treatment still in experimental stages, there is no specifically approved treatment for the particular Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus that caused this outbreak, declared on May 15. articles.title: Mali’s army recaptures town of Kidal
articles.author: Nicholas Mwangi
articles.content_excerpt: Mali’s armed forces have recaptured the northern city of Kidal following a large-scale military offensive conducted alongside Russia’s Africa Corps. It is a major development in the government’s efforts to restore state control over territory held by armed groups. The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa ) announced that their troops consolidated their operational deployment in Kidal on October 7, 2026, under Operation Dougoukoloko, following several days of airstrikes and coordinated air and ground operations against the Azawad Liberation Front (FLA) and Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM), an armed group affiliated with al-Qaeda. articles.title: Ansar Allah has the upper hand in escalating conflict with Saudi Arabia
articles.author: Aseel Saleh
articles.content_excerpt: Three months after Saudi Arabia resumed its aggression against Yemen’s Ansar Allah-led government by attacking Sanaa International Airport in July, the conflict continues to spiral. Saudi-backed forces claimed that they managed to cut off the main road connecting the Red Sea port city of Mokha with the Bab al-Mandeb strait on Monday, October 12, in a bid to reverse Ansar Allah’s major territorial gains along the Red Sea coast. This came after Ansar Allah launched an intensified military operation that resulted in encircling Yemen’s southwestern city of Taiz last week. Taiz has been under the control of the Saudi-backed Yemeni government for roughly the last ten years. As Yemen’s third-largest city, the encirclement of Taiz constitutes a critical development in the country’s armed conflict

articles.title: Political crisis in Pakistan deepens with dismissal of PTI-led provincial government
articles.author: Abdul Rahman
articles.content_excerpt: Large-scale protests broke out in different parts of Pakistan’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) province on Monday, October 12, after the federal government dismissed its elected government and imposed the centralized Governor’s rule. articles.title: “Musk”: Alex Gibney on New Film, Legal Threats & Elon Musk Spending $366M to Help GOP in Midterms
articles.content_excerpt: We speak with the Academy Award-winning director Alex Gibney about his new documentary Musk , an expansive, nearly four-hour examination of the world’s first trillionaire and how he has amassed unprecedented power in business, technology and politics. articles.title: Remembering Peter D. Thomas (1973–2026)
articles.author: Panagiotis Sotiris
articles.content_excerpt: It is with immense sadness and grief that we share the news of the death of our comrade, friend and long-standing member of the Historical Materialism Editorial Board Peter D. Thomas. Peter passed away due to a heart-attack on 11 October 2026, just after he had turned 53. With an academic background in philosophy and literature from his studies in Australia, having obtained a BA and an MA from the University of Queensland, he came to Europe to pursue his doctoral research in 2000. His PhD at the University of Amsterdam was supervised by Marcel van der Linden and Michael R. Krätke, and was awarded in 2008 despite efforts by right-wing members of the University to derail it. articles.title: The Land to Those Who Work It: Land Reform and Socialist Agriculture in the German Democratic Republic
articles.content_excerpt: About Studies on the DDR The German Democratic Republic (Deutsche Demokratische Republik, DDR) was a socialist state founded in East Germany in 1949 as a democratic, anti-fascist reaction to the Second World War and the subsequent restoration of monopoly capitalism in West Germany. The DDR represented a new Germany – one in which the land was redistributed, the means of production socialised, agricultural production organised into cooperatives, and significant advances made in gender equality, education, healthcare, and other areas of society.
